quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A solid white line means do not cross. A broken white line means you can cross to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes going opposite directions.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road widens ahead.
Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.
Lane reduction; the left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes only if you can do so safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Always make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat if there is a front passenger airbag.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point downward, it means they intend to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:

options.text: Only in an emergency.
If you are on an expressway.
If traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may cross to pass only if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is moving at a railroad crossing:

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close.
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
If you look carefully in both directions first.
Under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: On the freeway, you see a "Merging traffic" sign. You should:

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to prevent congestion.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When on a road with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering. If no one is next to you, move over one lane.

questions.question: What is the safest way to back up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio to get the attention of people nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Walk to the back of the vehicle first to check for children and small objects before you back up.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross safely. Be alert for pedestrians when driving through intersections or turning.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop if:

options.text: You need to unload packages.
You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
You need to let passengers out.
You stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's directions, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving while drunk is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Deer crossing.
Cattle crossing.
No right turn.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that deer may cross the road in this area.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other motorists.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the road.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between lanes is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: You are angry from something that happened at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly to stop thinking about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while angry or upset is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You cannot pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead.
You may pass only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white and rectangular with black markings. You must follow all instructions on regulatory signs. This sign means passing other vehicles is not allowed.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas next to and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. You must slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign (in this case, 35 mph).

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left—if the other driver corrects at the last second, you will still crash. Brake firmly to slow down. Every mile per hour slower reduces the impact.

questions.question: A green arrow turns into a solid green light. What do you do?

options.text: You can turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn anymore. You must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You do not have to turn in the arrow direction anymore.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow direction. However, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic first.

questions.question: Small children riding in a vehicle:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back seat.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must always be in a proper seat. They cannot stand while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be in a proper seat. They cannot stand while riding.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use the proper safety seat for your child.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far. Use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling helps other drivers know your plans and prevents accidents.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overpass ahead has limited height clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving opposite ways are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has limited height clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead is low. Do not go under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (in this case, 13 feet, 6 inches).

questions.question: When you increase your vehicle's speed:

options.text: You can see more around you.
You can see less around you.
It becomes easier to see cross traffic.
It does not change what you can see.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see less around you.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the less you can see around you. As you go faster, pay close attention to possible hazards.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: When turning right, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, move your car as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your car?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down on slippery or poor roads to keep control of your vehicle and be able to stop safely.

questions.question: What can you do from a center turn lane?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is only for left-turning vehicles from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or for driving straight through traffic.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the right curb or side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and gently slow down using the brakes. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back onto the pavement. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force the vehicle back.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to hazards.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react more slowly to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: Your wheels drop onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic as you re-enter the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane shifting.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Sharp turn, slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane shifting.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions. This yellow sign with black markings warns you that lanes are shifting. Follow the new lane path.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You may never stop your vehicle there.
You may park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You may stop to load or unload merchandise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Detour ahead.
Low shoulder.
Slippery when wet.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Detour ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers about construction zones ahead. This sign tells you that construction will change your normal driving route. Be ready to follow a redirected path.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: One-way road.
No right turn.
Exit.
Sharp right turn in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you there is a sharp right turn coming up on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Don't drink if you are going to drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest thing to do?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic controls, you must yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky behavior.
Nothing to worry about.
No more dangerous than normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well ahead of time. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process per hour?

options.text: Three drinks an hour.
One drink an hour.
Two drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. How fast you become impaired depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.
